title: Rolling Volume-Return Lead Cross-Correlation Predictive Fade (Lead-Lag Granger-Direction) — costed OOS (fail-closed, real quote volume)
path: R-B (validated real_quote_volume; no new blocked-family feed; C52 volume loading fixed so assets actually tested)
pre_stated_hypothesis: vrl_z = zscore(rolling Pearson corr(qvol[t], ret[t+k], W=48), ZLB=168) with lead k=1 and SIGNED returns. A lead-lag / Granger-direction statistic: does volume at t predict the signed future return? Genuinely different from C23/C40/C41 vol_z level (univariate), C42 expansion, C43 unsloped vol_z divergence, C44 vol_z ROC, C45 Amihud |ret|/volume pointwise ratio, C46 OBV signed-cumulative slopes, C47 up/down partition imbalance, C48 rolling STD of qvol (2nd-moment), C49 rolling excess kurtosis (4th-moment), C50 rolling skewness (3rd-moment), C51 rolling lag-1 autocorrelation (serial dependence), C52 contemporaneous cross-corr(qvol, |ret1|) co-movement (same t, magnitude-based). C53 uses a LEAD offset and SIGNED returns — a distinct lead-lag/predictive transform. Fade extreme predictive lead (vrl_z>=1.25 -> SHORT, vrl_z<=-1.25 -> LONG); |vrl_z|<1.25 no entry. Exit |vrl_z|<0.25 or hold>=12h or flip. t->t+1 execution. WF 720/168/168, cost grid 0-40bps, B&H benchmark on same OOS windows. Edge iff exposure>0 AND all slices OOS net>0 AND >B&H.
